To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prodynorphins are transcriptionally regulated by cAMP in PC12 cells through a CRE-like site located in the proximal promoter.
the prodynorphins are transcriptionally regulated through the CREB/CRE pathway.
c-Jun activation of the prodynorphine promoter occurs through the DYN-CRE3 site and that the c-Jun activation is mediated through the c-Jun transactivation domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of dynorphin expression and function.
the transcriptional regulation of the prodynorphine gene.
the identification of the transcription factors and cis-elements that are responsible for transcriptional regulation of the prodynorphins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c-Jun activation of the prodynorphins promoter is dependent upon phosphorylation of the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK).
c-Jun, in addition to CREB, is involved in the activation of prodynorphin transcription by the cAMP signal transduction pathway.
cAMP and c-Jun regulate prodynorphin transcription via the DYNCRE1 and DYNCRE3 sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a CRE site in the prod dynorphin gene promoter that binds c-Jun.
c-Jun, in concert with other factors, is a critical component of transcriptional regulation at the prodynorphian promoter.
the CREB/ATF family of transcription factors, including c-Jun, are important regulators of prodynorphin gene transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CREB/ATF1/ATF4/ATF5 family of transcription factors is involved in transcription of the prodynorphine gene.
the CREB family of transcription factors is important in the regulation of the prodynorphins.
we have identified a novel transcriptional regulatory element in the prodynophin promoter that is responsive to the activation of cAMP and cAMP-dependent protein kinase.
